candidates.current_role: Interim Fort Bend County Judge since April 2026 (appointment disputed); president and CEO, Tolunay-Wong Engineers
candidates.background: Daniel Wong, originally from Macau, is a civil engineer who earned bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees from the University of Houston and leads Tolunay-Wong Engineers, a firm he says employs more than 400 people. He served on the Sugar Land City Council from 2002 to 2008 and on the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board. He won the March 2026 Republican primary with about 54 percent, defeating incumbent KP George, and was named interim county judge in April 2026 after a visiting judge suspended George in a civil case. He is an elder at Fort Bend Community Church and lives in Sugar Land.

priorities.text: Says he is running to lower property taxes so tax bills go down, not just grow more slowly.
Campaigns on attracting employers to grow the commercial tax base and streamlining small business permitting.
Campaigns on infrastructure and flood protection, including repaving neglected roads and holding developers accountable for infrastructure.
Campaigns on workforce development, including skilled trades and apprenticeships.
Says he will support law enforcement and first responders and reduce crime through prevention and enforcement.
Says his priority is managing growth while protecting taxpayers and essential services.

promises.text: Says he will use the office to advocate for a cap on appraisal increases and to stop 'backdoor tax increases.'
Says he will audit government waste and prioritize fiscal discipline.
Says he will work with local authorities for reliable access to safe drinking water for all residents.

record.text: Was named interim county judge on April 10, 2026, after visiting Judge Jeth Jones suspended KP George in a civil case over residents' First Amendment complaints; the appointment was to last through that case.

After the civil case was dismissed in June 2026, the county attorney said his appointment ended June 17; he continued presiding, citing the Texas Constitution's holdover provision, and two commissioners voted to keep him presiding.

Filed suit against County Attorney Bridgette Smith-Lawson, arguing she exceeded her authority by declaring his appointment over; his attorneys say Commissioners Court approved his appointment through the end of 2026.
Says the county lowered its tax rate from 41.2 to 40.7 cents during his tenure.
Hired Trever Nehls as chief of staff at a six-figure salary, which Dexter McCoy said was more than double what other court employees earn.

notes.text: Endorsed by Gov. Greg Abbott, according to his campaign.
The Houston Chronicle editorial board endorsed him in the Republican primary; it endorsed his opponent in the general election.
A Texas Southern University poll conducted September 9 to October 2, 2026 found McCoy at 49 percent and Wong at 40 percent among registered voters.

q_county_tax.summary: Pledges to lower property tax bills, not just slow their growth, and says he would manage growth without raising taxes by seeking outside funding and growing the commercial base.

candidates.current_role: Galveston County Judge since 2011
candidates.background: Mark Henry was elected Galveston County Judge in 2010, the first Republican to hold the office since Reconstruction, and took office in 2011; he is seeking a fifth term. He defeated Chris Kinard in the March 2026 Republican primary with about 67 percent. He was an original chairman of the Gulf Coast Community Protection and Recovery District, formed after Hurricane Ike to study a coastal barrier.

priorities.text: Campaigns on lower taxes, public safety, less government and more efficiency, emergency management and infrastructure.
Says permanent drainage solutions will require federal, state and regional partnerships and billions of dollars of investment.

record.text: Says the county has adopted a property tax rate below the no-new-revenue rate every year since 2011, cutting the rate from about 0.63 to 0.32 per $100 valuation by 2025.
Says the county paid down debt and earned its first Aaa bond rating.
Says the Commissioners Court completed a countywide drainage study in 2021 and has spent hundreds of millions of dollars on road and drainage projects.
In 2021 the county declared a disaster over fentanyl deaths, created a Southern Border Taskforce that sent deputies to the border, and joined Operation Lone Star until it stood down in April 2025.
Says he increased the number of sheriff's and constable's officers on the streets.

notes.text: Galveston County, with Henry as a named defendant, was sued over the 2021 commissioners precinct map; a federal district court found it violated Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, and on August 1, 2024 the full Fifth Circuit reversed that ruling.
Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with about 67 percent of the vote over Chris Kinard.

q_county_tax.summary: Says the county has set its tax rate below the no-new-revenue rate every year since 2011, cutting the rate by nearly half, while urging voters to elect fiscally conservative local officials.
